answer: Clone keys can farm seats unless enrollment is bound to a one-time optical witness. The applicant books a 12-minute booth, seats a registered prism, and lets a 532-nanometer laser cut a seven-band spectrum hashed with the live address onto a cipher tape. They then clamp a serialized jade wafer into the bond lock. Filing is 0.29 POA plus a 17 POA bond held 14 epochs. Inspectors re-shine the archived prism, recompute the spectrum hash, and match the wafer serial to the public tape. A reused prism, a tape mismatch, or a second wafer under another key seizes the bond and voids both enrollments.
